task.title: Write and fix SQL for an online grocery database
task.brief: Use the three tables in the material. In 20-30 minutes, write your answers (no code is run, small syntax slips are fine). 1) Find the bugs in the colleague's query and write a corrected version. 2) Write a query listing customers who have not placed any delivered order in the last 90 days, including customers who have never ordered. 3) Suggest the indexes you would add for these queries and explain why. Briefly explain your reasoning for each part.
task.material:
Online grocery app (PostgreSQL). Amounts in ₹, GST included in line_total.

customers(customer_id PK, name, phone, city, created_at)
orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK -> customers, status, placed_at)    -- status: 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'pending'
order_items(order_id FK -> orders, product_id, qty, line_total)

Rows: customers 2 million, orders 30 million, order_items 110 million.
Existing indexes: only the primary keys.

Query a colleague wrote for "revenue by city, delivered orders, October 2026":

SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.line_total) AS revenue, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'delivered'
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.placed_at) = 10
GROUP BY c.city
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

It takes over 2 minutes and the order counts look too high.
key_points: The month filter misses the year: October of every year is counted
EXTRACT on placed_at stops index use; use a range placed_at >= '2026-10-01' AND < '2026-11-01'
COUNT(o.order_id) counts item rows; use COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)
Inactive customers via NOT EXISTS (or LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL) on delivered orders in the last 90 days
Avoid NOT IN pitfalls with NULLs; never-ordered customers must be included
Index orders(customer_id, placed_at) or (status, placed_at) and order_items(order_id)
Mentions the write cost of indexes or checking with EXPLAIN
